blocks.text: Andrew Scott-starring Elsinore is off to a nice start with a $240k limited opening on 6 screens in NY and LA. That’s a $40k per theater average as excellent exits polls bode well for the Focus Features’ film as it expands to 120 screens in top 25 markets starting Wednesday.

The true story of Ian Charleson, a gifted actor facing his own mortality with honesty, wit, and grace is “inspiring, and we could all use a movie that shows how you can live your life to the fullest even when you have obstacles in the way,” says Focus distribution chief Lisa Bunnell of the film, which has a 92% positive rating and an 80% recommend.

The film enters a crowded and dynamic period for the indie box office with a weekend of diverse debuts including a standout by Janus Films and Criterion’s exclusive 35mm tour of Paul Thomas Anderson’s Cameron Winter At Carnegie Hall . The concert film grossed $162k at just three locations for a $54k per-screen average, one of the year’s best. Shows were sold out at all theaters weeks in advance, and the 35mm-only meant additional showings couldn’t be added.

The tour continues through January, bringing the film to sixty of the largest historic theaters across the country for limited engagements, dozens of which have been sold out since October when the film premiered at the New York Film Festival. Theaters are selling exclusive merch at the shows. Up next is the Music Box in Chicago, The Castro in San Francisco, the AFI Silver Theatre outside Washington, D.C., and the TIFF Bell Lightbox.

God With Us , an event release from Variance Films in partnership with Blue Harbor Entertainment, saw a sizable $885k on 432 screens. The gross from writer-director Jimmy Jenkins’ modern day parable came largely without planned Saturday or Sunday evening showtimes, although theaters were adding them throughout the weekend . Originally programmed as a one weekend, three showtime event engagement, it will now remain in theaters throughout the holiday season.

Meanwhile, Club Kid from A24 grossed $1.4 million on 229 screens in limited release for a cume of $3.39 million. Jordan Firstman’s feature debut, with strong exits and word of mouth, continues to build ahead of a moderate nationwide expansion over Thanksgiving.

The distributor’s You Can See Everything remains in the top 10 (no. 6) after six weeks of release with a $2.5 million gross and a domestic cume of $93.4 million. The blockbuster doc by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim has crossed $100 million globally.
Limited : Neon’s Paper Tiger from James Gray grossed $336k in a week 2 expansion to 28 screens for a domestic cume of $622k. Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson and Miles Teller star.

Mubi’s release of Andrey Zvyagintsev’s Minotaur , winner of the Cannes Grand Prix, opened to $97k at 3 theaters in New York and Los Angeles to a $32.4k PTA — the highest for two-time Oscar-nominated director. The Hitchcockian thriller saw several sold out shows across the weekend at all three opening theaters in a crowded specialty marketplace heading into the Thanksgiving holiday.

Josephine from Sumerian Pictures , winner of the Grand Jury and Audience Awards in U.S. Dramatic Competition at Sundance, debuted to $84.2k on 4 screens in New York and Los Angeles. Will hold in limited release through the Thanksgiving holiday weekend before expanding nationwide Dec. 4. “We couldn’t be prouder of the initial response to Beth de Araújo’s visionary work, or more excited to share it nationally with moviegoers on the crest of such positive word of mouth,” said Sumerian President Rob Williams.
Pedro Almodovar’s Bitter Christmas from Sony Pictures Classics is eyeing $44k in week 2 at 11 locations for a cume of $99k.

Ash and Crayons from Briarcliff Entertainment opened one NYC screen, Angelika’s Village East, to $11.5k. The documentary by Evgeny Afineevsky follows the lives of seven Ukrainian children swept into the war with Russia. With no previews or advance shows, three Q&A screenings with the director and producer Kevin Goetz sold out and other screenings played at or near capacity. Bohdan Yermokhin, one of the film’s subjects, traveled from Ukraine for the Friday premiere. Expand to additional screens and markets in the coming weeks.

Wide : Peter Farrelly’s I Play Rocky from Amazon MGM starring Anthony Ippolito as a young Sylvester Stallone had a solid expansion with $9.3 million on 2,448 screens in week 3 for a $10.4 million gross. Exit data is super with an A+ Cinema Score, 97% in the top two boxes; 88% def recommend.
Godzilla Minus Zero from GKids is pushing $$2.7 million on 2,107 screens for the weekend in the no. 5 spot with a cume of $54.5 million in week 3.
Searchlight Pictures’ Wild Horse Nine is no. 7 in week 3 on 2,000 screens with a $2.5 million gross and a circa $18 million cume.
Fathom’s release of Laika’s animated Wildwood is hanging in at no. 9 on 1,341 screens with $2 million for a $28.4 million cume.

Indian films are out in force. As Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend from Sony Pictures (distributing the Prime Focus Studios film) becomes the highest-grossing Indian film of all time at the domestic box office, rounding out the top ten, another trio of Indian films is adding heft to the domestic box office. ENE Repeat from Prathyangira Cinemas booked $698k from 385 screens for a cume of $1.26 million; OM: Operation Mole from Prime Media Pictures debuted to $532k at 260 locations; and Aakasamlo Oka Tara from Sarigama Cinemas is at $408.5k with 200 locations (all three as per Rentrak).
Ramayana hit $28.4 million through Sunday with a weekend gross of just over $2 million at 681 theaters.
